page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v4 is a general-purpose server belonging to the DASv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 524 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-threaded tasks, such as bzip3 decompression, and specific workloads like ray tracing and image processing also register in the top tier. However, memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks (both read and write) falls into the average category, as do database operations, static web serving throughput, and single-threaded compression tasks.

While the server demonstrates strong capabilities in parallel processing and small-model LLM inference, it exhibits average performance for larger LLM models and standard database operations. The qualitative cost efficiency of this hardware profile is driven by its high resource density and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, making it suitable for multi-threaded applications, image processing, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring a balance of compute and memory.
description: Microsoft Azure D64as_v4 is a general-purpose server from the DASv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, running at 3.525 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of RAM and a 524 GB local SSD. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this x86_64 architecture server delivers strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth for cached small blocks, and strong multi-threaded decompression capabilities, placing it in the top 25% of benchmarks. Conversely, its uncached large-block memory bandwidth and database operations fall within the average range. This resource profile is suited for multi-threaded applications, image processing, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that require balanced compute and memory without dedicated GPU acceleration.
